ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a three-dimensional drawing of an approximate cube, with the original corners cut off; small triangular cross-sections appear at several visible corners, and the corners of the original larger square faces have been cut off, forming polygonal outlines. The problem statement says that all corners of the cube are cut off, so this also includes the invisible back corners in the figure. Reasoning: A cube has 8 vertices, and cutting off each vertex produces 1 new triangular face, so there are 8 triangular faces. The original 6 square faces of the cube, after the four corners of each face are truncated, become octagonal faces, so there are 6 octagonal faces. Calculating face-edge incidence count: the triangles contribute 8 × 3 = 24 face-edges, and the octagons contribute 6 × 8 = 48 face-edges, for a total of 24 + 48 = 72 face-edges. Each actual edge is shared by two faces, so the number of actual edges is 72 ÷ 2 = 36.

raw_record.question_text: A shape is made by cutting all the corners off a cube, as shown in the diagram. How many edges does the shape have?

method.method_draft: Use the diagram to recognize the solid as a cube with every one of its 8 corners truncated: the visible small triangular faces at corners indicate that each original cube vertex has been cut off, and each original square face has its four corners clipped. From the text, confirm that all corners of the cube are cut off, not just the visible ones. Count faces by type: 8 new triangular faces are created, one at each original cube corner, and the 6 original cube faces become octagonal faces. Count face-edge incidences: triangles contribute 8 × 3 = 24 edge-sides and octagons contribute 6 × 8 = 48 edge-sides, for 72 total face-edge incidences. Since every physical edge is shared by exactly two faces, divide by 2 to get 72/2 = 36 edges.
